topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, contextualizes the lecture series, and outlines the three core learning objectives on environmental cancer causes, mechanisms, and testing.

topics.label: The Nature of Cancer and Drivers of Mutation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and outline the balanced sources of mutations across endogenous processes, inherited predispositions, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey everyday environmental carcinogens, explore the debate over environmental causation versus random bad luck, and examine epidemiological and migrant data on geographic cancer variation.

topics.label: Biological and Molecular Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the diverse molecular and cellular mechanisms of carcinogenesis, including oncogenic pathogens, xenobiotic metabolic activation, physical DNA damage, tumor promotion via inflammation, and host developmental susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Determining Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic mutational signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo rodent assays, and in vitro Ames tests used to detect and prove carcinogen exposure.

topics.label: Concluding Summary and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by synthesizing environmental cancer risks, highlighting the challenges of carcinogenicity testing, and framing daily exposures as personal risk-benefit decisions.
